# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T test.ld -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul
# Probe fixtures: QEMU1-only, no vsim/QEMU2 phase. Used by shell tests
# that inspect the raw state file to verify plugin drain behavior.
PROBE_V_FIXTURES := probe_v_csr

RUNTIME_DIR     := runtime
RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump demo

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(PROBE_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are legacy (referenced only
# by EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp). They still build for completeness
# but are not in active CTest. All targets now share test.ld at 0x00100000.

# Switching-mode demo runner: builds the fixtures if needed, then walks
# T1..T7 from $(DEMO_DIR), printing a banner per mode and a final
# pass/fail tally. Honors FILTER=<regex> to subset the run.
demo: all
	@bash demo.sh

spin.elf: spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (test.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# Probe fixtures: pure asm, -march=rv64gcv (need V CSR names), no C runtime.
PROBE_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
$(PROBE_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(PROBE_V_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

# Roadmap: run all 7 demos on one RVV GEMM workload

## Goal

Every demo under `tests/demos/` (T1..T7) should showcase its switching mechanism on
the SAME RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
modes": CSR, PC, icount, and SimPoint (shown via its profile / slice / archive /
loop stages, T4-T7). Today demos split between `rt_c_v_regs` and `icount_spin`.

We reuse the existing GEMM `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` (16x16x16 outer-product,

## Why two builds of one source

`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:

- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.

Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.

- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.

- Orchestrator CSR-drain is marker-driven: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py:33` passes

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Acceptance test for gemm_modes.md: every demo runs the SAME RVV GEMM
# (rt_c_v_matmul.c), so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
# modes". Marker-driven demos (csr / pc / archive / simpoint) use the MARKED
# build; count-driven demos (icount / bbv / slice) use the MARKERLESS twin.
#
# Pure parsing of each demo's default FIXTURE -- no artifacts, no round-trip.
# Goes fully green only once F3..F8 have swapped every demo; until then it
# names exactly which demos still point at an old fixture.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# demo file -> expected default fixture
declare -A EXPECT=(
  [demo_csr_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_pc_oneshot.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_icount_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_bbv_profile.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul_free
  [demo_archive_replay.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
  [demo_simpoint_loop.sh]=rt_c_v_matmul
)

# Pull the default fixture name from the demo's FIXTURE= assignment, whether
# written `FIXTURE=foo ...` (csr/pc inline env) or `FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-foo}"`.
# \K drops everything matched so far, leaving just the fixture token.
fixture_of() {
  grep -oP 'FIXTURE=(?:"?\$\{FIXTURE:-)?\K[A-Za-z0-9_]+' "$1" | head -1
}

bad=0
for demo in "${!EXPECT[@]}"; do
  f="$SCRIPT_DIR/$demo"
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "[FAIL] missing demo $demo"; bad=1; continue; }
  got=$(fixture_of "$f")
  want="${EXPECT[$demo]}"
  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
    echo "[ok] $demo -> $got"
  else
    echo "[FAIL] $demo uses '$got', expected '$want'"
    bad=1
  fi
done

if [ "$bad" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL test_demos_use_gemm: not every demo runs the GEMM yet"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS test_demos_use_gemm: all 7 demos run the GEMM workload"

# Roadmap: run all 7 demos on one RVV GEMM workload

## Goal

Every demo under `tests/demos/` (T1..T7) should showcase its switching mechanism on
the SAME RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
modes": CSR, PC, icount, and SimPoint (shown via its profile / slice / archive /
loop stages, T4-T7). Today demos split between `rt_c_v_regs` and `icount_spin`.

We reuse the existing GEMM `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` (16x16x16 outer-product,
`__riscv_vle32` / `__riscv_vmacc_vx` / `__riscv_vse32`).

## Why two builds of one source

`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:

- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.

Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.

### Confirmed findings (probed on the built artifacts)
- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.
  The kernel is inlined at `-O1`, so a PC-range assertion has no symbol to anchor on.
  Fix: mark `vmatmul_kernel` `noinline` (also keeps it in the ROI per
  `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:49-51`).
- Orchestrator CSR-drain is marker-driven: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py:33` passes
  the plugin only `outfile=...`; `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:237` sets replay
  `trigger_kind="csr"`. So T6 and T7 must use the MARKED build.

## Fixture mapping (target state)

| Demo | Mode     | Stage / role           | Build      | ELF                    |
|------|----------|------------------------|------------|------------------------|
| T1   | CSR      | -                      | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T2   | PC       | -                      | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T3   | icount   | -                      | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T4   | SimPoint | Stage 1: bbv profile   | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T5   | SimPoint | Stage 2: slice-consume | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T6   | SimPoint | Stage 3: archive       | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T7   | SimPoint | headline: full loop    | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |

T7 keeps current behavior: its small slice/icount targets profile the crt0+init
prefix BEFORE the enter marker (same regime as today's `rt_c_v_regs`); the kernel
runs in the SimPoint replay leg.

# Roadmap: run all 7 demos on one RVV GEMM workload

## Goal

Every demo under `tests/demos/` (T1..T7) should showcase its switching mechanism on
the SAME RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
modes": CSR, PC, icount, and SimPoint (shown via its profile / slice / archive /
loop stages, T4-T7). Today demos split between `rt_c_v_regs` and `icount_spin`.

We reuse the existing GEMM `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` (16x16x16 outer-product,
`__riscv_vle32` / `__riscv_vmacc_vx` / `__riscv_vse32`).

## Why two builds of one source

`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:

- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.

Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.

### Confirmed findings (probed on the built artifacts)
- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.
  The kernel is inlined at `-O1`, so a PC-range assertion has no symbol to anchor on.
  Fix: mark `vmatmul_kernel` `noinline` (also keeps it in the ROI per
  `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:49-51`).
- Orchestrator CSR-drain is marker-driven: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py:33` passes
  the plugin only `outfile=...`; `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:237` sets replay
  `trigger_kind="csr"`. So T6 and T7 must use the MARKED build.

## Fixture mapping (target state)

| Demo | Mode     | Stage / role           | Build      | ELF                    |
|------|----------|------------------------|------------|------------------------|
| T1   | CSR      | -                      | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T2   | PC       | -                      | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T3   | icount   | -                      | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T4   | SimPoint | Stage 1: bbv profile   | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T5   | SimPoint | Stage 2: slice-consume | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T6   | SimPoint | Stage 3: archive       | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T7   | SimPoint | headline: full loop    | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |

T7 keeps current behavior: its small slice/icount targets profile the crt0+init
prefix BEFORE the enter marker (same regime as today's `rt_c_v_regs`); the kernel
runs in the SimPoint replay leg.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-icount_spin}"
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"

MODE_LABEL="Icount switching (M3)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: ${FIXTURE} (CSR-less tight loop)"

hybrid_resolve_paths

SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-icount-rt.XXXXXX)

STATE_V=$(mktemp)

read_u64() { python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$1', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek($2); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
"; }

  echo "[demo M3] FAIL: QEMU1 expected exit 200, got $QRC"

fi

fi

PC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 16)
PC_Q_HEX=$(printf "0x%x" "$PC_Q")
if [ "$PC_Q_HEX" != "0x100002" ] && [ "$PC_Q_HEX" != "0x100004" ]; then
  echo "[demo M3] FAIL: QEMU1 drained pc=$PC_Q_HEX not in icount_spin loop"; exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (icount mode): instruction-count switching on the RVV GEMM workload.
#
# Whole-program mode: both legs drain by retired-instruction count alone, with
# no CSR markers in the workload:
#
#   QEMU1 + plugin icount=N1    -> drain at insn N1.
#   vsim --hybrid-icount N2     -> drain N2 insns later.
#
# Workload is the MARKERLESS GEMM twin rt_c_v_matmul_free (200 back-to-back
# 16x16x16 GEMMs, no csrwi 0x7C0). icount IS the only drain trigger -- the
# default CSR matcher has nothing to match. There is no natural end-of-program
# drain here (the demo stops vsim mid-kernel by count), so it asserts the
# round-trip DRAINS at both ends with both PCs landing inside vmatmul_kernel.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      markerless fixture (default: rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)
#   QEMU_ICOUNT   plugin icount drain target (default: 10000)
#   VSIM_ICOUNT   vsim icount drain target  (default: 5000)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"

MODE_LABEL="icount mode (samples a whole-program window)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: ${FIXTURE} (markerless RVV GEMM, 200 reps)"
echo "QEMU1 trigger: plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT"
echo "vsim  trigger: --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT  (CSR matcher disabled)"
echo "=========================================================="

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Resolve the GEMM kernel's address range so the drain checks assert the count
# target landed inside vmatmul_kernel (replaces the old icount_spin's hardcoded
# 0x100002/0x100004 loop PCs). readelf -sW: $2=value(hex) $3=size $8=name.
RE="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
RE="${RE:-riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
read KLO KSZ < <("$RE" -sW "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$8=="vmatmul_kernel"{print strtonum("0x"$2),$3; exit}')
if [ -z "${KLO:-}" ] || [ -z "${KSZ:-}" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: could not resolve vmatmul_kernel range from $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1
fi
pc_in_kernel() { awk -v p="$1" -v lo="$KLO" -v sz="$KSZ" 'BEGIN{exit !(p>=lo && p<lo+sz)}'; }
echo "  vmatmul_kernel: $(printf '0x%x..0x%x' "$KLO" "$((KLO+KSZ))")"

SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-icount-rt.XXXXXX)
STATE_Q=$(mktemp)
STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)

truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"

read_u64() { python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$1', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek($2); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
"; }

echo "[demo icount 1/2] QEMU1 + plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e

  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_Q,icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
QRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 expected exit 200, got $QRC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_Q" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 state empty"; exit 1
fi

PC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 16)
if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_Q"; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 drained pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") not in vmatmul_kernel"; exit 1
fi
echo "  QEMU1 drain: pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") (in kernel)"

# vsim resumes from the QEMU drain and attaches the SAME shared mmap so the
# GEMM matrices QEMU1 wrote to .bss survive (mirrors tests/e2e.sh).
echo "[demo icount 2/2] vsim --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e
timeout 120 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_Q" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_V" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  >"$VSIM_LOG" 2>&1
VRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$VRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim expected exit 200, got $VRC"
  tail -20 "$VSIM_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_V" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim state empty"; exit 1
fi

PC_V=$(read_u64 "$STATE_V" 16)
if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_V"; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim drained pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_V") not in vmatmul_kernel"; exit 1
fi
echo "  vsim drain: pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_V") (in kernel)"

# Window cycles: the vsim mcycle delta over the measured window (mcycle@624).
# vsim restores mcycle from the QEMU drain then counts real cycles, so
# vsim - qemu is the window's cycle count.
MC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 624)
MC_V=$(read_u64 "$STATE_V" 624)
echo "  window_cycles: $((MC_V - MC_Q))  (vsim mcycle=$MC_V - qemu mcycle=$MC_Q)"

echo "[demo icount] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): both drains inside vmatmul_kernel"

# Roadmap: run all 7 demos on one RVV GEMM workload

## Goal

Every demo under `tests/demos/` (T1..T7) should showcase its switching mechanism on
the SAME RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
modes": CSR, PC, icount, and SimPoint (shown via its profile / slice / archive /
loop stages, T4-T7). Today demos split between `rt_c_v_regs` and `icount_spin`.

`__riscv_vle32` / `__riscv_vmacc_vx` / `__riscv_vse32`).

## Why two builds of one source

`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:

- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.

Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.

- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.

  `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:49-51`).
- Orchestrator CSR-drain is marker-driven: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py:33` passes
  the plugin only `outfile=...`; `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:237` sets replay
  `trigger_kind="csr"`. So T6 and T7 must use the MARKED build.

| T3   | icount   | -                      | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T4   | SimPoint | Stage 1: bbv profile   | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T5   | SimPoint | Stage 2: slice-consume | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T6   | SimPoint | Stage 3: archive       | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T7   | SimPoint | headline: full loop    | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |

prefix BEFORE the enter marker (same regime as today's `rt_c_v_regs`); the kernel
runs in the SimPoint replay leg.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo T5: slice-consume entry (M5) + icount exit (M3) on a CSR-less workload.
#
# Demonstrates that the orchestrator can use DIFFERENT trigger modes for
# the entry and exit of the same vsim window:
#
#   QEMU + plugin: slice=N,slice_at=K -> drains at end of slice K (M5).
#   vsim         : --hybrid-icount M  -> drains after M retired insns (M3).
#
# Workload is icount_spin.elf (CSR-less, predictable tight loop), so neither
# side can use the csrwi 0x7C0 marker. There is no natural QEMU2 exit
# because the workload spins forever; this demo asserts the round-trip
# DRAINS correctly at both ends. M8 is covered by T1 / T2 / T6.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      CSR-less fixture (default: icount_spin.elf)
#   SLICE         insns per slice    (default: 1000)
#   SLICE_AT      0-based slice index for drain (default: 1)
#   ICOUNT_FALLBACK QEMU plugin safety upper bound (default: 10000)
#   VSIM_ICOUNT   insns vsim runs before exit drain (default: 5000)
#   SIMPTS        optional simpts file from T4; if set, slice_at picked
#                 from its first row (first column) instead of SLICE_AT env.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-icount_spin}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-1000}"
SLICE_AT_ENV="${SLICE_AT:-1}"
ICOUNT_FALLBACK="${ICOUNT_FALLBACK:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"
SIMPTS="${SIMPTS:-}"

# If a SIMPTS file from T4 is provided, pick the first listed slice index.
# Otherwise fall back to SLICE_AT env (default 1).
if [ -n "$SIMPTS" ] && [ -s "$SIMPTS" ]; then
  SLICE_AT=$(awk 'NR==1{print $1}' "$SIMPTS")
  SLICE_AT_SRC="simpts(first row of $SIMPTS)"
else
  SLICE_AT="$SLICE_AT_ENV"
  SLICE_AT_SRC="env SLICE_AT"
fi

MODE_LABEL="Slice-consume entry (M5) + icount exit (M3)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Workload: icount_spin (CSR-less tight loop)"
echo "Entry: QEMU plugin slice=$SLICE slice_at=$SLICE_AT (from $SLICE_AT_SRC)"
echo "Exit : vsim --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT"
echo "=========================================================="

hybrid_resolve_paths

EXPECTED_QEMU_INSN=$(( (SLICE_AT + 1) * SLICE ))
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-slice-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_Q=$(mktemp)
STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_Q" "$STATE_V" "$QEMU_LOG" "$VSIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

echo "[demo M5 1/2] QEMU + plugin: drain at end of slice $SLICE_AT (insn $EXPECTED_QEMU_INSN)"
set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_Q,slice=$SLICE,slice_at=$SLICE_AT,icount=$ICOUNT_FALLBACK" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
QRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU expected exit 200, got $QRC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_Q" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU state file empty"
  exit 1
fi

# Verify drain happened at the slice boundary (plugin logs idx=K+1 target=K).
EXPECTED_IDX=$((SLICE_AT + 1))
if ! grep -qE "slice-consume drain \(idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT\)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU drain not at slice boundary idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Drained PC must be inside icount_spin loop body (0x100004 / 0x100008).
PC_Q=$(python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$STATE_Q', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(16); print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0]))
")
if [ "$PC_Q" != "0x100002" ] && [ "$PC_Q" != "0x100004" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU drained pc=$PC_Q not in icount_spin loop"
  exit 1
fi
echo "  QEMU drain: idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT pc=$PC_Q"

echo "[demo M5 2/2] vsim: resume + drain after $VSIM_ICOUNT retired insns"
set +e
timeout 60 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_Q" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_V" \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  >"$VSIM_LOG" 2>&1
VRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$VRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: vsim expected exit 200, got $VRC"
  tail -20 "$VSIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_V" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: vsim state file empty"
  exit 1
fi

PC_V=$(python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$STATE_V', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(16); print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0]))
")
if [ "$PC_V" != "0x100002" ] && [ "$PC_V" != "0x100004" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: vsim drained pc=$PC_V not in icount_spin loop"
  exit 1
fi
echo "  vsim drain: after $VSIM_ICOUNT insns pc=$PC_V"

echo "[demo M5] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): both drains inside icount_spin ROI"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (SimPoint stage: slice-consume): drain QEMU at a slice boundary, then
# measure a window in vsim -- on the RVV GEMM workload.
#
# Shows the orchestrator using DIFFERENT trigger modes for the entry and exit
# of the same vsim window:
#
#   QEMU + plugin: slice=N,slice_at=K -> drains at end of slice K.
#   vsim         : --hybrid-icount M  -> drains after M retired insns.
#
# Workload is the MARKERLESS GEMM twin rt_c_v_matmul_free (no csrwi 0x7C0), so
# neither side can use the marker -- slice/icount ARE the only triggers. There
# is no natural end-of-program drain (the demo stops vsim mid-kernel by count);

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-1000}"
SLICE_AT_ENV="${SLICE_AT:-1}"
ICOUNT_FALLBACK="${ICOUNT_FALLBACK:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"
SIMPTS="${SIMPTS:-}"

  SLICE_AT=$(awk 'NR==1{print $1}' "$SIMPTS")
  SLICE_AT_SRC="simpts(first row of $SIMPTS)"
else
  SLICE_AT="$SLICE_AT_ENV"
  SLICE_AT_SRC="env SLICE_AT"

echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"

# Demo T5: slice-consume entry (M5) + icount exit (M3) on a CSR-less workload.

# the entry and exit of the same vsim window:
#
#   QEMU + plugin: slice=N,slice_at=K -> drains at end of slice K (M5).
#   vsim         : --hybrid-icount M  -> drains after M retired insns (M3).
#
# Workload is icount_spin.elf (CSR-less, predictable tight loop), so neither
# side can use the csrwi 0x7C0 marker. There is no natural QEMU2 exit
# because the workload spins forever; this demo asserts the round-trip
# DRAINS correctly at both ends. M8 is covered by T1 / T2 / T6.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>

#   VSIM_ICOUNT   insns vsim runs before exit drain (default: 5000)
#   SIMPTS        optional simpts file from T4; if set, slice_at picked
#                 from its first row (first column) instead of SLICE_AT env.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-icount_spin}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-1000}"
SLICE_AT_ENV="${SLICE_AT:-1}"
ICOUNT_FALLBACK="${ICOUNT_FALLBACK:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"
SIMPTS="${SIMPTS:-}"

# If a SIMPTS file from T4 is provided, pick the first listed slice index.
# Otherwise fall back to SLICE_AT env (default 1).
if [ -n "$SIMPTS" ] && [ -s "$SIMPTS" ]; then
  SLICE_AT=$(awk 'NR==1{print $1}' "$SIMPTS")
  SLICE_AT_SRC="simpts(first row of $SIMPTS)"
else
  SLICE_AT="$SLICE_AT_ENV"
  SLICE_AT_SRC="env SLICE_AT"
fi

MODE_LABEL="Slice-consume entry (M5) + icount exit (M3)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Workload: icount_spin (CSR-less tight loop)"
echo "Entry: QEMU plugin slice=$SLICE slice_at=$SLICE_AT (from $SLICE_AT_SRC)"
echo "Exit : vsim --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT"
echo "=========================================================="

hybrid_resolve_paths

EXPECTED_QEMU_INSN=$(( (SLICE_AT + 1) * SLICE ))
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-slice-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_Q=$(mktemp)
STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_Q" "$STATE_V" "$QEMU_LOG" "$VSIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

echo "[demo M5 1/2] QEMU + plugin: drain at end of slice $SLICE_AT (insn $EXPECTED_QEMU_INSN)"
set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_Q,slice=$SLICE,slice_at=$SLICE_AT,icount=$ICOUNT_FALLBACK" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
QRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU expected exit 200, got $QRC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_Q" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU state file empty"
  exit 1
fi

# Verify drain happened at the slice boundary (plugin logs idx=K+1 target=K).
EXPECTED_IDX=$((SLICE_AT + 1))
if ! grep -qE "slice-consume drain \(idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT\)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then

  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

PC_Q=$(python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$STATE_Q', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(16); print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0]))
")
if [ "$PC_Q" != "0x100002" ] && [ "$PC_Q" != "0x100004" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU drained pc=$PC_Q not in icount_spin loop"
  exit 1
fi
echo "  QEMU drain: idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT pc=$PC_Q"

  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \

  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_V" ]; then

  exit 1

PC_V=$(python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$STATE_V', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(16); print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0]))
")
if [ "$PC_V" != "0x100002" ] && [ "$PC_V" != "0x100004" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: vsim drained pc=$PC_V not in icount_spin loop"
  exit 1
fi
echo "  vsim drain: after $VSIM_ICOUNT insns pc=$PC_V"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo T4: BBV-emit switching mode (M4) + SimPoint clustering integration.
#
# QEMU + plugin runs icount_spin.elf with bbv_out=PATH,slice=N,icount=M.
# Plugin writes one SimPoint .bb row per N retired insns; expected
# rows = M/N. Then tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint clusters the .bb file
# and produces simpts (slice -> cluster) + weights (cluster -> mass).
#
# Outputs are persisted under $WORKDIR (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
# so T5/T7 can consume them. WORKDIR is printed on PASS.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF      a CSR-less fixture (default: icount_spin.elf)
#   SIMPOINT_BIN  the built simpoint clustering binary
#   WORKDIR       persistent dir for bbv/simpts/weights (default: mktemp -d)
#   SLICE         insns per BBV row (default: 1000)
#   ICOUNT        total insns before drain (default: 10000)
#   MAXK          simpoint -maxK (default: 2; tiny BBVs need conservative K)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-icount_spin}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
SIMPOINT_BIN="${SIMPOINT_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint}"
WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-$(mktemp -d -t demo-bbv-XXXXXX)}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-1000}"
ICOUNT="${ICOUNT:-10000}"
MAXK="${MAXK:-2}"

MODE_LABEL="BBV emit + SimPoint cluster (M4)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Workload: ${FIXTURE} (tight 2-insn loop, CSR-less)"
echo "Plugin: bbv_out=...,slice=$SLICE,icount=$ICOUNT"
echo "Workdir: $WORKDIR"
echo "=========================================================="

if [ ! -x "$SIMPOINT_BIN" ]; then
  echo "[demo M4] SKIP: $SIMPOINT_BIN not built"
  exit 77
fi

mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"
BBV_OUT="$WORKDIR/icount_spin.bb"
SIMPTS="$WORKDIR/simpts"
WEIGHTS="$WORKDIR/weights"
STATE_OUT="$WORKDIR/state_qemu.bin"
QEMU_LOG="$WORKDIR/qemu.log"
SP_LOG="$WORKDIR/simpoint.log"

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-bbv-shared.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

EXPECTED_ROWS=$((ICOUNT / SLICE))

echo "[demo M4 1/3] QEMU + plugin: emit BBV ($EXPECTED_ROWS rows expected)"
set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_OUT,icount=$ICOUNT,bbv_out=$BBV_OUT,slice=$SLICE" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo M4] FAIL: QEMU expected exit 200, got $RC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

ROWS=$(wc -l < "$BBV_OUT")
if [ "$ROWS" -ne "$EXPECTED_ROWS" ]; then
  echo "[demo M4] FAIL: expected $EXPECTED_ROWS BBV rows, got $ROWS"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[demo M4 2/3] SimPoint cluster: maxK=$MAXK"
set +e
"$SIMPOINT_BIN" -loadFVFile "$BBV_OUT" -maxK "$MAXK" -dim 2 \
  -saveSimpoints "$SIMPTS" -saveSimpointWeights "$WEIGHTS" \
  >"$SP_LOG" 2>&1
SP_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$SP_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo M4] FAIL: simpoint exit $SP_RC"
  tail -20 "$SP_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$SIMPTS" ] || [ ! -s "$WEIGHTS" ]; then
  echo "[demo M4] FAIL: simpoint output empty (simpts=$(wc -c <"$SIMPTS") weights=$(wc -c <"$WEIGHTS"))"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[demo M4 3/3] Chosen phases:"
echo "  simpts (slice_idx cluster_id):"
awk '{printf "    %s\n", $0}' "$SIMPTS"
echo "  weights (mass cluster_id):"
awk '{printf "    %s\n", $0}' "$WEIGHTS"

# Informational: weights should sum to ~1.0 (no hard assert; simpoint
# may emit weights in unnormalised form for some -maxK paths).
SUM=$(awk '{s+=$1} END{printf "%.4f", s}' "$WEIGHTS")
echo "  weight sum: $SUM"

echo "[demo M4] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): rows=$ROWS, clusters=$(wc -l <"$SIMPTS"), workdir=$WORKDIR"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo T7: full SimPoint pipeline (M4 -> M5 -> M6 -> M7).
#
# Centerpiece demo showing every switching mode in the production
# SimPoint flow:
#
#   M4 - profile pass: QEMU+plugin bbv_out=,slice=N -> .bb file
#   ---  cluster      : tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint -loadFVFile ...
#   M5 - per-phase    : QEMU+plugin slice=N,slice_at=K,outfile= -> drain
#   M6 - archive      : write snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}
#   M7 - replay       : orchestrator replay-checkpoint --resume-with vsim
#
# Workload: rt_c_v_regs (C-level Tier-2 fixture with natural csrwi
# 0x7C0,1 exit marker, so replay's hardcoded vsim+csr trigger drains
# naturally without --hybrid-icount tuning).
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      Tier-2 fixture (default: rt_c_v_regs.elf)
#   SIMPOINT_BIN  tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
#   WORKDIR       persistent dir (default: mktemp -d)
#   SLICE         insns per BBV row / per slice (default: 200)
#   PROFILE_ICOUNT plugin icount fallback for profile pass (default: 8000)
#   PHASE_ICOUNT  plugin icount fallback per phase run (default: 8000)
#   MAXK          simpoint -maxK (default: 2)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_regs}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
SIMPOINT_BIN="${SIMPOINT_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint}"
WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-$(mktemp -d -t demo-simpoint-XXXXXX)}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-20}"
PROFILE_ICOUNT="${PROFILE_ICOUNT:-2000}"
PHASE_ICOUNT="${PHASE_ICOUNT:-2000}"
MAXK="${MAXK:-2}"
# Defaults are tuned for rt_c_v_regs which reaches csrwi 0x7C0,0 after
# ~200-400 insns of QEMU1 startup. slice=20 gives ~15 BBV rows, enough
# for simpoint to find 2 clusters. Tune via env for other fixtures.

MODE_LABEL="Full SimPoint loop (M4 -> M5 -> M6 -> M7)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Workload: $(basename "$VSIM_ELF")"
echo "Slice: $SLICE insns; profile icount: $PROFILE_ICOUNT; maxK: $MAXK"
echo "Workdir: $WORKDIR"
echo "=========================================================="

if [ ! -x "$SIMPOINT_BIN" ]; then
  echo "[demo T7] SKIP: $SIMPOINT_BIN not built"; exit 77
fi
if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[demo T7] SKIP: python3 not found"; exit 77
fi

mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"
BBV="$WORKDIR/profile.bb"
SIMPTS="$WORKDIR/simpts"
WEIGHTS="$WORKDIR/weights"
SP_LOG="$WORKDIR/simpoint.log"
SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))

# ---- M4: profile pass ----------------------------------------------------
echo "[demo T7 1/4] M4 profile: bbv_out=,slice=$SLICE,icount=$PROFILE_ICOUNT"
SHM_PROFILE=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-t7-profile.XXXXXX)
PROFILE_STATE="$WORKDIR/profile_state.bin"
PROFILE_LOG="$WORKDIR/profile_qemu.log"
truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM_PROFILE"
trap 'rm -f "$SHM_PROFILE"' EXIT

set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM_PROFILE,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$PROFILE_STATE,bbv_out=$BBV,slice=$SLICE,icount=$PROFILE_ICOUNT" \
  >"$PROFILE_LOG" 2>&1
PRC=$?
set -e
rm -f "$SHM_PROFILE"

if [ "$PRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo T7] FAIL: profile QEMU expected exit 200, got $PRC"
  tail -20 "$PROFILE_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$BBV" ]; then
  echo "[demo T7] FAIL: BBV file empty"; exit 1
fi
BBV_ROWS=$(wc -l < "$BBV")
echo "  $BBV_ROWS BBV rows -> $BBV"

# ---- M4-cluster: simpoint -----------------------------------------------
echo "[demo T7 2/4] cluster: simpoint -maxK $MAXK -dim 2"
set +e
"$SIMPOINT_BIN" -loadFVFile "$BBV" -maxK "$MAXK" -dim 2 \
  -saveSimpoints "$SIMPTS" -saveSimpointWeights "$WEIGHTS" \
  >"$SP_LOG" 2>&1
SP_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$SP_RC" -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$SIMPTS" ]; then
  echo "[demo T7] FAIL: simpoint rc=$SP_RC; simpts size=$(wc -c <"$SIMPTS" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  tail -20 "$SP_LOG"; exit 1
fi
NUM_PHASES=$(wc -l <"$SIMPTS")
echo "  $NUM_PHASES cluster representatives:"
awk '{printf "    slice=%s cluster=%s\n", $1, $2}' "$SIMPTS"

# ---- M5+M6: per-phase drain + archive -----------------------------------
echo "[demo T7 3/4] for each phase: drain at slice_at=K + archive"
PHASE_INDICES=$(awk '{print $1}' "$SIMPTS")
declare -a ARCHIVES=()
for K in $PHASE_INDICES; do
  SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm "vsim-t7-phase${K}.XXXXXX")
  truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"
  STATE="$WORKDIR/phase_${K}_state.bin"
  Q_LOG="$WORKDIR/phase_${K}_qemu.log"

  set +e
  timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
    -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,slice=$SLICE,slice_at=$K,icount=$PHASE_ICOUNT" \
    >"$Q_LOG" 2>&1
  QRC=$?
  set -e

  if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
    rm -f "$SHM"
    echo "[demo T7] FAIL: phase $K QEMU exit $QRC"; tail -20 "$Q_LOG"; exit 1
  fi

  # M6: write snap/<K>/{state.bin, mem, meta.json} via the orchestrator's
  # write_archive helper (the canonical M6 entry point used by F9).
  SNAP="$WORKDIR/snap/$K"
  set +e
  PYTHONPATH="$TOP_ROOT/tools" python3 - <<PY
from pathlib import Path
from orchestrator.checkpoint import write_archive
write_archive(
    Path("$SNAP"),
    state_path=Path("$STATE"),
    mmap_path=Path("$SHM"),
    mmap_size=$SHM_SIZE,
    elf_path="tests/fixtures/$(basename "$VSIM_ELF")",
    source_step_index=0,
    cpu_variant="ax45mpv_premium",
    region_id=f"snap/$K",
    slice_index=$K,
)
PY
  AR_RC=$?
  set -e
  rm -f "$SHM"
  if [ "$AR_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "[demo T7] FAIL: write_archive for phase $K (rc=$AR_RC)"; exit 1
  fi
  for f in state.bin mem meta.json; do
    if [ ! -s "$SNAP/$f" ]; then
      echo "[demo T7] FAIL: $SNAP/$f missing/empty"; exit 1
    fi
  done
  ARCHIVES+=("$SNAP")
  echo "  phase $K archived -> $SNAP"
done

# ---- M7: replay each archive --------------------------------------------
echo "[demo T7 4/4] for each archive: replay-checkpoint --resume-with vsim"
REPLAY_OK=0
for SNAP in "${ARCHIVES[@]}"; do
  K=$(basename "$SNAP")
  REPLAY_WD="$WORKDIR/replay_$K"
  R_LOG="$WORKDIR/replay_${K}.log"
  mkdir -p "$REPLAY_WD"
  set +e
  PYTHONPATH="$TOP_ROOT/tools" VSIM_QEMU="$VSIM_QEMU" \
    VSIM_PLUGIN="$VSIM_PLUGIN" VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BIN" \
    timeout 120 python3 -m orchestrator.main replay-checkpoint "$SNAP" \
      --resume-with vsim --project-root "$TOP_ROOT" --workdir "$REPLAY_WD" \
      >"$R_LOG" 2>&1
  R_RC=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$R_RC" -eq 0 ] || [ "$R_RC" -eq 200 ]; then
    echo "  phase $K: replay OK (rc=$R_RC)"
    REPLAY_OK=$((REPLAY_OK + 1))
  else
    echo "  phase $K: replay FAILED (rc=$R_RC)"
    tail -15 "$R_LOG"
  fi
done

if [ "$REPLAY_OK" -ne "$NUM_PHASES" ]; then
  echo "[demo T7] FAIL: $REPLAY_OK/$NUM_PHASES replays succeeded"
  exit 1
fi

# ---- whole-program cycle estimate (the SimPoint headline number) --------
# The chain above validates the M4->M7 plumbing; the whole-program cycle
# figure comes from `hsim estimate` (profile -> cluster -> per-phase vsim
# measure -> weighted CPI x N_total). Reuses the same slice/maxK.
echo "[demo T7 estimate] whole-program cycle estimate via ./hsim estimate"
EST_LOG="$WORKDIR/estimate.log"
set +e
VSIM_QEMU="$VSIM_QEMU" VSIM_PLUGIN="$VSIM_PLUGIN" VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BIN" \
  "$TOP_ROOT/hsim" estimate "$VSIM_ELF" \
    --slice "$SLICE" --max-k "$MAXK" --icount "$PROFILE_ICOUNT" >"$EST_LOG" 2>&1
EST_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$EST_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo T7] FAIL: hsim estimate rc=$EST_RC"; tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi
EST_CYCLES=$(grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' "$EST_LOG" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
if [ "${EST_CYCLES:-0}" -le 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo T7] FAIL: hsim estimate produced no positive estimated_cycles"
  tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi
echo "  estimated_cycles=$EST_CYCLES  (whole-program, weighted CPI)"

echo "[demo T7] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): bbv_rows=$BBV_ROWS phases=$NUM_PHASES replays_ok=$REPLAY_OK estimated_cycles=$EST_CYCLES workdir=$WORKDIR"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo T7: full SimPoint pipeline (M4 -> M5 -> M6 -> M7).
#
# Centerpiece demo showing every switching mode in the production
# SimPoint flow:
#
#   M4 - profile pass: QEMU+plugin bbv_out=,slice=N -> .bb file
#   ---  cluster      : tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint -loadFVFile ...
#   M5 - per-phase    : QEMU+plugin slice=N,slice_at=K,outfile= -> drain
#   M6 - archive      : write snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}
#   M7 - replay       : orchestrator replay-checkpoint --resume-with vsim
#
# Workload: rt_c_v_regs (C-level Tier-2 fixture with natural csrwi
# 0x7C0,1 exit marker, so replay's hardcoded vsim+csr trigger drains
# naturally without --hybrid-icount tuning).
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      Tier-2 fixture (default: rt_c_v_regs.elf)
#   SIMPOINT_BIN  tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
#   WORKDIR       persistent dir (default: mktemp -d)
#   SLICE         insns per BBV row / per slice (default: 200)
#   PROFILE_ICOUNT plugin icount fallback for profile pass (default: 8000)
#   PHASE_ICOUNT  plugin icount fallback per phase run (default: 8000)
#   MAXK          simpoint -maxK (default: 2)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
SIMPOINT_BIN="${SIMPOINT_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint}"
WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-$(mktemp -d -t demo-simpoint-XXXXXX)}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-20}"
PROFILE_ICOUNT="${PROFILE_ICOUNT:-2000}"
PHASE_ICOUNT="${PHASE_ICOUNT:-2000}"
MAXK="${MAXK:-2}"
# Defaults are tuned for rt_c_v_regs which reaches csrwi 0x7C0,0 after
# ~200-400 insns of QEMU1 startup. slice=20 gives ~15 BBV rows, enough
# for simpoint to find 2 clusters. Tune via env for other fixtures.

MODE_LABEL="Full SimPoint loop (M4 -> M5 -> M6 -> M7)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Workload: $(basename "$VSIM_ELF")"
echo "Slice: $SLICE insns; profile icount: $PROFILE_ICOUNT; maxK: $MAXK"
echo "Workdir: $WORKDIR"
echo "=========================================================="

if [ ! -x "$SIMPOINT_BIN" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] SKIP: $SIMPOINT_BIN not built"; exit 77
fi
if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] SKIP: python3 not found"; exit 77
fi

mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"
BBV="$WORKDIR/profile.bb"
SIMPTS="$WORKDIR/simpts"
WEIGHTS="$WORKDIR/weights"
SP_LOG="$WORKDIR/simpoint.log"
SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))

# ---- M4: profile pass ----------------------------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 1/4] M4 profile: bbv_out=,slice=$SLICE,icount=$PROFILE_ICOUNT"
SHM_PROFILE=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-t7-profile.XXXXXX)
PROFILE_STATE="$WORKDIR/profile_state.bin"
PROFILE_LOG="$WORKDIR/profile_qemu.log"
truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM_PROFILE"
trap 'rm -f "$SHM_PROFILE"' EXIT

set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM_PROFILE,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$PROFILE_STATE,bbv_out=$BBV,slice=$SLICE,icount=$PROFILE_ICOUNT" \
  >"$PROFILE_LOG" 2>&1
PRC=$?
set -e
rm -f "$SHM_PROFILE"

if [ "$PRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: profile QEMU expected exit 200, got $PRC"
  tail -20 "$PROFILE_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$BBV" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: BBV file empty"; exit 1
fi
BBV_ROWS=$(wc -l < "$BBV")
echo "  $BBV_ROWS BBV rows -> $BBV"

# ---- M4-cluster: simpoint -----------------------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 2/4] cluster: simpoint -maxK $MAXK -dim 2"
set +e
"$SIMPOINT_BIN" -loadFVFile "$BBV" -maxK "$MAXK" -dim 2 \
  -saveSimpoints "$SIMPTS" -saveSimpointWeights "$WEIGHTS" \
  >"$SP_LOG" 2>&1
SP_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$SP_RC" -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$SIMPTS" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: simpoint rc=$SP_RC; simpts size=$(wc -c <"$SIMPTS" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  tail -20 "$SP_LOG"; exit 1
fi
NUM_PHASES=$(wc -l <"$SIMPTS")
echo "  $NUM_PHASES cluster representatives:"
awk '{printf "    slice=%s cluster=%s\n", $1, $2}' "$SIMPTS"

# ---- M5+M6: per-phase drain + archive -----------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 3/4] for each phase: drain at slice_at=K + archive"
PHASE_INDICES=$(awk '{print $1}' "$SIMPTS")
declare -a ARCHIVES=()
for K in $PHASE_INDICES; do
  SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm "vsim-t7-phase${K}.XXXXXX")
  truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"
  STATE="$WORKDIR/phase_${K}_state.bin"
  Q_LOG="$WORKDIR/phase_${K}_qemu.log"

  set +e
  timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
    -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,slice=$SLICE,slice_at=$K,icount=$PHASE_ICOUNT" \
    >"$Q_LOG" 2>&1
  QRC=$?
  set -e

  if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
    rm -f "$SHM"
    echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: phase $K QEMU exit $QRC"; tail -20 "$Q_LOG"; exit 1
  fi

  # M6: write snap/<K>/{state.bin, mem, meta.json} via the orchestrator's
  # write_archive helper (the canonical M6 entry point used by F9).
  SNAP="$WORKDIR/snap/$K"
  set +e
  PYTHONPATH="$TOP_ROOT/tools" python3 - <<PY
from pathlib import Path
from orchestrator.checkpoint import write_archive
write_archive(
    Path("$SNAP"),
    state_path=Path("$STATE"),
    mmap_path=Path("$SHM"),
    mmap_size=$SHM_SIZE,
    elf_path="tests/fixtures/$(basename "$VSIM_ELF")",
    source_step_index=0,
    cpu_variant="ax45mpv_premium",
    region_id=f"snap/$K",
    slice_index=$K,
)
PY
  AR_RC=$?
  set -e
  rm -f "$SHM"
  if [ "$AR_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: write_archive for phase $K (rc=$AR_RC)"; exit 1
  fi
  for f in state.bin mem meta.json; do
    if [ ! -s "$SNAP/$f" ]; then
      echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: $SNAP/$f missing/empty"; exit 1
    fi
  done
  ARCHIVES+=("$SNAP")
  echo "  phase $K archived -> $SNAP"
done

# ---- M7: replay each archive --------------------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 4/4] for each archive: replay-checkpoint --resume-with vsim"
REPLAY_OK=0
for SNAP in "${ARCHIVES[@]}"; do
  K=$(basename "$SNAP")
  REPLAY_WD="$WORKDIR/replay_$K"
  R_LOG="$WORKDIR/replay_${K}.log"
  mkdir -p "$REPLAY_WD"
  set +e
  PYTHONPATH="$TOP_ROOT/tools" VSIM_QEMU="$VSIM_QEMU" \
    VSIM_PLUGIN="$VSIM_PLUGIN" VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BIN" \
    timeout 120 python3 -m orchestrator.main replay-checkpoint "$SNAP" \
      --resume-with vsim --project-root "$TOP_ROOT" --workdir "$REPLAY_WD" \
      >"$R_LOG" 2>&1
  R_RC=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$R_RC" -eq 0 ] || [ "$R_RC" -eq 200 ]; then
    echo "  phase $K: replay OK (rc=$R_RC)"
    REPLAY_OK=$((REPLAY_OK + 1))
  else
    echo "  phase $K: replay FAILED (rc=$R_RC)"
    tail -15 "$R_LOG"
  fi
done

if [ "$REPLAY_OK" -ne "$NUM_PHASES" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: $REPLAY_OK/$NUM_PHASES replays succeeded"
  exit 1
fi

# ---- whole-program cycle estimate (the SimPoint headline number) --------
# The chain above validates the M4->M7 plumbing; the whole-program cycle
# figure comes from `hsim estimate` (profile -> cluster -> per-phase vsim
# measure -> weighted CPI x N_total). Reuses the same slice/maxK.
echo "[demo simpoint estimate] whole-program cycle estimate via ./hsim estimate"
EST_LOG="$WORKDIR/estimate.log"
set +e
VSIM_QEMU="$VSIM_QEMU" VSIM_PLUGIN="$VSIM_PLUGIN" VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BIN" \
  "$TOP_ROOT/hsim" estimate "$VSIM_ELF" \
    --slice "$SLICE" --max-k "$MAXK" --icount "$PROFILE_ICOUNT" >"$EST_LOG" 2>&1
EST_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$EST_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: hsim estimate rc=$EST_RC"; tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi
EST_CYCLES=$(grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' "$EST_LOG" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
if [ "${EST_CYCLES:-0}" -le 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: hsim estimate produced no positive estimated_cycles"
  tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (SimPoint mode): headline whole-program flow on the RVV GEMM.
#
# The SimPoint-driven mode profiles the run into slices, clusters them into
# representative phases, measures each phase, and weight-combines into a
# whole-program cycle estimate. Its stages:
#
#   profile : QEMU+plugin bbv_out=,slice=N -> .bb file
#   cluster : tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint -loadFVFile ...
#   per-phase: QEMU+plugin slice=N,slice_at=K,outfile= -> drain
#   archive : write snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}
#   replay  : orchestrator replay-checkpoint --resume-with vsim
#   estimate: ./hsim estimate -> weighted-CPI whole-program cycle figure
#
# Workload: rt_c_v_matmul (marked RVV GEMM with natural csrwi 0x7C0,1 exit
# marker, so replay's hardcoded vsim+csr trigger drains naturally without
# --hybrid-icount tuning). As with the kernel-mode demos, the small
# slice/icount targets profile the crt0+init prefix BEFORE the enter marker;
# the GEMM kernel itself runs in the replay leg.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      Tier-2 fixture (default: rt_c_v_regs.elf)
#   SIMPOINT_BIN  tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
#   WORKDIR       persistent dir (default: mktemp -d)
#   SLICE         insns per BBV row / per slice (default: 200)
#   PROFILE_ICOUNT plugin icount fallback for profile pass (default: 8000)
#   PHASE_ICOUNT  plugin icount fallback per phase run (default: 8000)
#   MAXK          simpoint -maxK (default: 2)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
SIMPOINT_BIN="${SIMPOINT_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint}"
WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-$(mktemp -d -t demo-simpoint-XXXXXX)}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-20}"
PROFILE_ICOUNT="${PROFILE_ICOUNT:-2000}"
PHASE_ICOUNT="${PHASE_ICOUNT:-2000}"
MAXK="${MAXK:-2}"
# Defaults are tuned for rt_c_v_regs which reaches csrwi 0x7C0,0 after
# ~200-400 insns of QEMU1 startup. slice=20 gives ~15 BBV rows, enough
# for simpoint to find 2 clusters. Tune via env for other fixtures.

MODE_LABEL="Full SimPoint loop (M4 -> M5 -> M6 -> M7)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Workload: $(basename "$VSIM_ELF")"
echo "Slice: $SLICE insns; profile icount: $PROFILE_ICOUNT; maxK: $MAXK"
echo "Workdir: $WORKDIR"
echo "=========================================================="

if [ ! -x "$SIMPOINT_BIN" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] SKIP: $SIMPOINT_BIN not built"; exit 77
fi
if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] SKIP: python3 not found"; exit 77
fi

mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"
BBV="$WORKDIR/profile.bb"
SIMPTS="$WORKDIR/simpts"
WEIGHTS="$WORKDIR/weights"
SP_LOG="$WORKDIR/simpoint.log"
SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))

# ---- M4: profile pass ----------------------------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 1/4] M4 profile: bbv_out=,slice=$SLICE,icount=$PROFILE_ICOUNT"
SHM_PROFILE=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-t7-profile.XXXXXX)
PROFILE_STATE="$WORKDIR/profile_state.bin"
PROFILE_LOG="$WORKDIR/profile_qemu.log"
truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM_PROFILE"
trap 'rm -f "$SHM_PROFILE"' EXIT

set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM_PROFILE,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$PROFILE_STATE,bbv_out=$BBV,slice=$SLICE,icount=$PROFILE_ICOUNT" \
  >"$PROFILE_LOG" 2>&1
PRC=$?
set -e
rm -f "$SHM_PROFILE"

if [ "$PRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: profile QEMU expected exit 200, got $PRC"
  tail -20 "$PROFILE_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$BBV" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: BBV file empty"; exit 1
fi
BBV_ROWS=$(wc -l < "$BBV")
echo "  $BBV_ROWS BBV rows -> $BBV"

# ---- M4-cluster: simpoint -----------------------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 2/4] cluster: simpoint -maxK $MAXK -dim 2"
set +e
"$SIMPOINT_BIN" -loadFVFile "$BBV" -maxK "$MAXK" -dim 2 \
  -saveSimpoints "$SIMPTS" -saveSimpointWeights "$WEIGHTS" \
  >"$SP_LOG" 2>&1
SP_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$SP_RC" -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$SIMPTS" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: simpoint rc=$SP_RC; simpts size=$(wc -c <"$SIMPTS" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  tail -20 "$SP_LOG"; exit 1
fi
NUM_PHASES=$(wc -l <"$SIMPTS")
echo "  $NUM_PHASES cluster representatives:"
awk '{printf "    slice=%s cluster=%s\n", $1, $2}' "$SIMPTS"

# ---- M5+M6: per-phase drain + archive -----------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 3/4] for each phase: drain at slice_at=K + archive"
PHASE_INDICES=$(awk '{print $1}' "$SIMPTS")
declare -a ARCHIVES=()
for K in $PHASE_INDICES; do
  SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm "vsim-t7-phase${K}.XXXXXX")
  truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"
  STATE="$WORKDIR/phase_${K}_state.bin"
  Q_LOG="$WORKDIR/phase_${K}_qemu.log"

  set +e
  timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
    -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,slice=$SLICE,slice_at=$K,icount=$PHASE_ICOUNT" \
    >"$Q_LOG" 2>&1
  QRC=$?
  set -e

  if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
    rm -f "$SHM"
    echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: phase $K QEMU exit $QRC"; tail -20 "$Q_LOG"; exit 1
  fi

  # M6: write snap/<K>/{state.bin, mem, meta.json} via the orchestrator's
  # write_archive helper (the canonical M6 entry point used by F9).
  SNAP="$WORKDIR/snap/$K"
  set +e
  PYTHONPATH="$TOP_ROOT/tools" python3 - <<PY
from pathlib import Path
from orchestrator.checkpoint import write_archive
write_archive(
    Path("$SNAP"),
    state_path=Path("$STATE"),
    mmap_path=Path("$SHM"),
    mmap_size=$SHM_SIZE,
    elf_path="tests/fixtures/$(basename "$VSIM_ELF")",
    source_step_index=0,
    cpu_variant="ax45mpv_premium",
    region_id=f"snap/$K",
    slice_index=$K,
)
PY
  AR_RC=$?
  set -e
  rm -f "$SHM"
  if [ "$AR_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: write_archive for phase $K (rc=$AR_RC)"; exit 1
  fi
  for f in state.bin mem meta.json; do
    if [ ! -s "$SNAP/$f" ]; then
      echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: $SNAP/$f missing/empty"; exit 1
    fi
  done
  ARCHIVES+=("$SNAP")
  echo "  phase $K archived -> $SNAP"
done

# ---- M7: replay each archive --------------------------------------------
echo "[demo simpoint 4/4] for each archive: replay-checkpoint --resume-with vsim"
REPLAY_OK=0
for SNAP in "${ARCHIVES[@]}"; do
  K=$(basename "$SNAP")
  REPLAY_WD="$WORKDIR/replay_$K"
  R_LOG="$WORKDIR/replay_${K}.log"
  mkdir -p "$REPLAY_WD"
  set +e
  PYTHONPATH="$TOP_ROOT/tools" VSIM_QEMU="$VSIM_QEMU" \
    VSIM_PLUGIN="$VSIM_PLUGIN" VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BIN" \
    timeout 120 python3 -m orchestrator.main replay-checkpoint "$SNAP" \
      --resume-with vsim --project-root "$TOP_ROOT" --workdir "$REPLAY_WD" \
      >"$R_LOG" 2>&1
  R_RC=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$R_RC" -eq 0 ] || [ "$R_RC" -eq 200 ]; then
    echo "  phase $K: replay OK (rc=$R_RC)"
    REPLAY_OK=$((REPLAY_OK + 1))
  else
    echo "  phase $K: replay FAILED (rc=$R_RC)"
    tail -15 "$R_LOG"
  fi
done

if [ "$REPLAY_OK" -ne "$NUM_PHASES" ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: $REPLAY_OK/$NUM_PHASES replays succeeded"
  exit 1
fi

# ---- whole-program cycle estimate (the SimPoint headline number) --------
# The chain above validates the M4->M7 plumbing; the whole-program cycle
# figure comes from `hsim estimate` (profile -> cluster -> per-phase vsim
# measure -> weighted CPI x N_total). Reuses the same slice/maxK.
echo "[demo simpoint estimate] whole-program cycle estimate via ./hsim estimate"
EST_LOG="$WORKDIR/estimate.log"
set +e
VSIM_QEMU="$VSIM_QEMU" VSIM_PLUGIN="$VSIM_PLUGIN" VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BIN" \
  "$TOP_ROOT/hsim" estimate "$VSIM_ELF" \
    --slice "$SLICE" --max-k "$MAXK" --icount "$PROFILE_ICOUNT" >"$EST_LOG" 2>&1
EST_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$EST_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: hsim estimate rc=$EST_RC"; tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi
EST_CYCLES=$(grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' "$EST_LOG" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
if [ "${EST_CYCLES:-0}" -le 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: hsim estimate produced no positive estimated_cycles"
  tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi
echo "  estimated_cycles=$EST_CYCLES  (whole-program, weighted CPI)"

echo "[demo simpoint] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): bbv_rows=$BBV_ROWS phases=$NUM_PHASES replays_ok=$REPLAY_OK estimated_cycles=$EST_CYCLES workdir=$WORKDIR"

  if [ "$R_RC" -eq 0 ] || [ "$R_RC" -eq 200 ]; then
    echo "  phase $K: replay OK (rc=$R_RC)"
    REPLAY_OK=$((REPLAY_OK + 1))
  else

    tail -15 "$R_LOG"
  fi
done

  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: $REPLAY_OK/$NUM_PHASES replays succeeded"
  exit 1
fi

# ---- whole-program cycle estimate (the SimPoint headline number) --------
# The chain above validates the M4->M7 plumbing; the whole-program cycle
# figure comes from `hsim estimate` (profile -> cluster -> per-phase vsim
# measure -> weighted CPI x N_total). Reuses the same slice/maxK.
echo "[demo simpoint estimate] whole-program cycle estimate via ./hsim estimate"

set +e
VSIM_QEMU="$VSIM_QEMU" VSIM_PLUGIN="$VSIM_PLUGIN" VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BIN" \
  "$TOP_ROOT/hsim" estimate "$VSIM_ELF" \
    --slice "$SLICE" --max-k "$MAXK" --icount "$PROFILE_ICOUNT" >"$EST_LOG" 2>&1
EST_RC=$?
set -e
if [ "$EST_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: hsim estimate rc=$EST_RC"; tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi
EST_CYCLES=$(grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' "$EST_LOG" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
if [ "${EST_CYCLES:-0}" -le 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo simpoint] FAIL: hsim estimate produced no positive estimated_cycles"
  tail -20 "$EST_LOG"; exit 1
fi
echo "  estimated_cycles=$EST_CYCLES  (whole-program, weighted CPI)"

echo "[demo simpoint] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): bbv_rows=$BBV_ROWS phases=$NUM_PHASES replays_ok=$REPLAY_OK estimated_cycles=$EST_CYCLES workdir=$WORKDIR"

163	## 3. PC mode - same kernel, no source edit
164	
165	### What it does
166	
167	Same round-trip as CSR mode, but the trigger is a PC value, not an opcode
168	match. The harness resolves each boundary - taken from `ROI_START` /
169	`ROI_END`, which default to the symbols `_hybrid_enter_pc` and
170	`_hybrid_exit_pc` - to an address (a `0x` value is used verbatim; a name is
171	looked up with `nm`, see `tests/lib/roi.sh`), then passes:
172	
173	- `enter_pc=0x<addr>` to the QEMU plugin (QEMU1 drains there)
174	- `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<addr>` to vsim (vsim drains there)
175	
176	CSR-mode matchers are bypassed; the `csrwi 0x7C0, *` instructions become
177	inert. This proves you can hand off WITHOUT modifying the source: point the
178	boundaries at any function or address the binary already has.
179	
180	### Inputs
181	
182	- Same fixture as CSR mode (`rt_c_v_regs`). With the defaults, the ELF must
183	  define `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc` (the C-level fixtures all
184	  do). To target a different region, set `ROI_START` / `ROI_END` (or
185	  `./hsim run --roi-start/--roi-end`) to any symbol or `0x` address - then
186	  no marker symbols are needed at all.
187	
188	### Cycle figure
189	
190	Identical to CSR mode: kernel cycles = vsim `mcycle` - QEMU1 `mcycle`
191	(offset 624). The boundaries differ, the measurement does not.
192	
193	```sh
194	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs TRIGGER_MODE=pc CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 \
195	  bash tests/e2e.sh
196	```

208	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
209	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
210	EXIT_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
211	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
212	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')
213	
214	# QEMU plugin arg
215	... -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC

219	```

222

233	retires - so they also report the same kernel cycle delta.

237	## 4. icount mode - a sampled window (single boundary)
238	
239	### What it does
240	
241	Both legs switch on retired-instruction count alone. No CSR, no PC symbol -
242	suitable for CSR-less workloads (an infinite spin loop, a benchmark you
243	cannot edit, a raw blob).
244	
245	- QEMU plugin: `icount=N` -> drain at the N-th retired insn (fast-forward).
246	- vsim: `--hybrid-icount M` -> drain M insns after resume (measure).
247	
248	This is a **single boundary** on each side: fast-forward N in QEMU, measure
249	M in vsim. There is no warmup window - vsim starts the measured window with
250	a cold cache and pipeline, so the cycle figure includes that cold-start
251	cost.
252	
253	### Inputs
254	
255	- Any ELF; `icount_spin.elf` is the canonical CSR-less fixture.
256	
257	### Output and cycle figure
258	
259	Both QEMU1 and vsim exit 200 with a non-empty state file. There is no QEMU2
260	phase for `icount_spin` because it spins forever (no natural semihosting
261	exit). Window cycles = `mcycle(vsim drain) - mcycle(QEMU drain)`, each read
262	at offset 624 of the two drained state files.
263	
264	### Run it
265	
266	```sh
267	bash tests/demos/demo_icount_roundtrip.sh
268	```
269	
270	Override targets:
271	
272	```sh
273	QEMU_ICOUNT=20000 VSIM_ICOUNT=8000 \
274	  bash tests/demos/demo_icount_roundtrip.sh
275	```
276	
277	### Exercise 3
278	
279	Predict where the drained PC will land for `icount_spin.elf`. The loop body
280	has two RVC instructions at PCs `0x100002` and `0x100004`. Run with
281	`VSIM_ICOUNT=5000`; the drained PC should be one of those two values. Read
282	the demo's `read_u64` helper - it pulls the PC from offset 16. The same
283	helper at offset 624 gives `mcycle`; subtract the QEMU and vsim values to
284	get the window's cycle count.
285	
286	---
287	
288	## 5. SimPoint-driven mode - the whole program
289	
290	### What it does
291	
292	Real programs run billions of instructions; you cannot cycle-simulate all
293	of them. SimPoint samples instead: profile the run into fixed slices,
294	cluster the slices into a few representative phases, measure each phase like
295	icount mode, then weight-combine the per-phase cycles into a whole-program
296	estimate. SimPoint mode is icount mode applied at several clustering-chosen
297	points.
298	
299	### Stages
300	
301	1. **Profile (BBV).** The plugin emits one Basic-Block-Vector row per slice
302	   of N retired insns into a SimPoint `.bb` file (`bbv_out=`, `slice=N`).
303	2. **Cluster.** `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint` reads the `.bb` and clusters
304	   the rows into K representative phases: a `simpts` file (one slice index
305	   per cluster) and a `weights` file (one weight per cluster).
306	3. **Per phase.** For each representative slice K: QEMU drains at the end of
307	   slice K (`slice=N`, `slice_at=K`), vsim resumes and measures that slice's
308	   cycles (the `mcycle` delta).
309	4. **Archive / replay (optional).** A drained state plus its shared mmap can
310	   be packaged into `snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}` and replayed on
311	   another host. This is the checkpoint plumbing, not a separate mode.
312	5. **Combine.** `estimated_cycles = N_total * sum(weight_i * CPI_i)`, where
313	   `CPI_i = delta_mcycle_i / insns_measured` and `N_total` is the whole
314	   program's retired-instruction count.
315	
316	### Cycle figure (the headline)
317	
318	`hsim estimate` runs every stage and prints the whole-program number:
319	
320	```sh
321	./hsim estimate tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf --slice 20 --icount 0 --max-k 2
322	```
323	
324	Last line:
325	
326	```
327	estimated_cycles=<N>  (N=<insns>, weighted_CPI=<x.xxx>)
328	```
329	
330	`--icount 0` profiles to program exit, so `N` is the true total
331	instruction count. Run `./hsim estimate -h` for all flags.
332	
333	### Stage drill-downs
334	
335	Each stage also has a standalone demo, useful when debugging one piece:
336	
337	```sh
338	# Stage 1+2: profile + cluster
339	WORKDIR=/tmp/sp-profile bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
340	# Stage 3: consume one representative slice on vsim
341	SIMPTS=/tmp/sp-profile/simpts \
342	  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
343	# Stage 4: archive a drained state and replay it
344	WORKDIR=/tmp/sp-archive bash tests/demos/demo_archive_replay.sh
345	```
346	
347	### Headline demo: the full loop
348	
349	`demo_simpoint_loop.sh` chains all stages on `rt_c_v_regs.elf`:
350	
351	```sh
352	WORKDIR=/tmp/sp bash tests/demos/demo_simpoint_loop.sh
353	```
354	
355	It profiles, clusters into representative phases, drains each phase, archives
356	it, and replays each archive on vsim (which finishes naturally on
357	`csrwi 0x7C0,1`). The loop validates the end-to-end replay chain; use
358	`hsim estimate` above when you want the whole-program cycle estimate printed.
359	
360	### Exercise 4 (capstone)
361	
362	Pick a fixture (e.g. `rt_c_matmul`) and tune `--slice` so the profile pass
363	yields between 10 and 30 slices, then run `hsim estimate` on it. Goals:
364	
365	- Find the `--slice` that gives a good cluster count (try 20, 50, 200).
366	- Read off `estimated_cycles` and `weighted_CPI`.
367	- Compare the estimate's wall-clock against a full CSR-mode run of the same
368	  kernel. SimPoint should be similar for tiny fixtures; the speedup shows on
369	  real workloads.
370	
371	---
372	
373	## 6. Running the whole suite
374	
375	### Sequential runner (with banners)
376	
377	```sh
378	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/tests/fixtures
379	make demo
380	# or
381	bash demo.sh
382	# subset:
383	FILTER='csr|pc'  bash demo.sh
384	FILTER=simpoint  bash demo.sh
385	```
386	
387	The suite ends with a PASS/FAIL/SKIP tally over the per-mode demos (the CSR,
388	PC, and icount headline demos, plus the SimPoint stage and loop demos).
389	
390	### Parallel runner (scripts/run_e2e.sh)
391	
392	```sh
393	JOBS=8 FILTER=demo bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
394	```
395	
396	This runs every `demo_*.sh` (and every other e2e fixture matching the
397	default suite) in parallel under a FIFO job pool. The summary line gets a
398	`demo Np/Mf/Ks` column.

   slice K (`slice=N`, `slice_at=K`), vsim resumes and measures that slice's
   cycles (the `mcycle` delta).
4. **Archive / replay (optional).** A drained state plus its shared mmap can
   be packaged into `snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}` and replayed on
   another host. This is the checkpoint plumbing, not a separate mode.
5. **Combine.** `estimated_cycles = N_total * sum(weight_i * CPI_i)`, where
   `CPI_i = delta_mcycle_i / insns_measured` and `N_total` is the whole
   program's retired-instruction count.

### Cycle figure (the headline)

`hsim estimate` runs every stage and prints the whole-program number:

```sh
./hsim estimate tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf --slice 20 --icount 0 --max-k 2
```

Last line:

```
estimated_cycles=<N>  (N=<insns>, weighted_CPI=<x.xxx>)
```

`--icount 0` profiles to program exit, so `N` is the true total
instruction count. Run `./hsim estimate -h` for all flags.

### Stage drill-downs

Each stage also has a standalone demo, useful when debugging one piece:

```sh
# Stage 1+2: profile + cluster
WORKDIR=/tmp/sp-profile bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
# Stage 3: consume one representative slice on vsim
SIMPTS=/tmp/sp-profile/simpts \
  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
# Stage 4: archive a drained state and replay it
WORKDIR=/tmp/sp-archive bash tests/demos/demo_archive_replay.sh
```

### Headline demo: the full loop

`demo_simpoint_loop.sh` chains all stages on `rt_c_v_regs.elf`:

```sh
WORKDIR=/tmp/sp bash tests/demos/demo_simpoint_loop.sh
```

It profiles, clusters into representative phases, drains each phase, archives
it, and replays each archive on vsim (which finishes naturally on
`csrwi 0x7C0,1`). The loop validates the end-to-end replay chain; use
`hsim estimate` above when you want the whole-program cycle estimate printed.

### Exercise 4 (capstone)

Pick a fixture (e.g. `rt_c_matmul`) and tune `--slice` so the profile pass
yields between 10 and 30 slices, then run `hsim estimate` on it. Goals:

- Find the `--slice` that gives a good cluster count (try 20, 50, 200).
- Read off `estimated_cycles` and `weighted_CPI`.
- Compare the estimate's wall-clock against a full CSR-mode run of the same
  kernel. SimPoint should be similar for tiny fixtures; the speedup shows on
  real workloads.

---

## 6. Running the whole suite

### Sequential runner (with banners)

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/tests/fixtures
make demo
# or
bash demo.sh
# subset:
FILTER='csr|pc'  bash demo.sh
FILTER=simpoint  bash demo.sh
```

The suite ends with a PASS/FAIL/SKIP tally over the per-mode demos (the CSR,
PC, and icount headline demos, plus the SimPoint stage and loop demos).

### Parallel runner (scripts/run_e2e.sh)

```sh
JOBS=8 FILTER=demo bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

This runs every `demo_*.sh` (and every other e2e fixture matching the
default suite) in parallel under a FIFO job pool. The summary line gets a
`demo Np/Mf/Ks` column.
